title: Tuples Quiz
description: Review tuple basics, unpacking values, and why tuples are immutable.

questions.explanation: Parentheses with commas define tuples; square brackets define lists.
The trailing comma makes a one-element tuple.

questions.prompt: Tuples are immutable—you cannot reassign their elements after creation.
questions.explanation: You cannot do t[0] = 5 on a tuple; create a new tuple instead.

options: Assigns 3 to x and 7 to y
questions.explanation: Tuple unpacking matches positions to variable names on the left.

options: Error because tuples cannot be indexed
questions.explanation: Tuples support indexing and slicing like lists, but not assignment.
Comma-separated values without brackets form a tuple (tuple packing).

questions.prompt: A single value in parentheses like `(99)` is a tuple.
questions.explanation: (99) is just the integer 99; you need a comma: (99,) for a one-item tuple.
Tuple objects do not support item assignment.
len counts elements in the tuple.

questions.prompt: Which unpacks the first two items from `(10, 20, 30)` into a and b?
questions.explanation: You need the same number of targets as values, or use * or _ for extras.
+ concatenates tuples into a new tuple.

questions.prompt: Tuples can be used as keys in dictionaries if all elements are hashable.
questions.explanation: Immutable hashable tuples work as dict keys; lists cannot.
*rest collects remaining items into a list during unpacking.

questions.prompt: Why might you choose a tuple over a list for coordinates (x, y)?
options: Fixed size and immutability signal the pair should not change
Tuples are always faster to type
questions.explanation: Immutability makes tuples good for fixed collections used as records or dict keys.
Slicing a tuple returns a new tuple.
count tells how many times a value appears in the tuple.

questions.prompt: tuple([1, 2]) converts a list into a tuple.
questions.explanation: tuple() builds a tuple from any iterable.

questions.prompt: What is `a` after `a, b = b, a` if `a = 1` and `b = 2`?
questions.explanation: Right side evaluates as (2, 1) before assignment, swapping values without a temp variable.

questions.prompt: Can a tuple contain a mutable list?
options: Yes, but the tuple itself still cannot replace that list element
No, tuples may only hold numbers
Yes, and then the whole tuple becomes mutable
questions.explanation: The tuple cannot rebind t[0], but a list inside can still be modified in place.
Repeating a tuple with * concatenates copies.
